sentences.en: Wildfires are becoming an increasing menace in the western United States, with Southern California being the hardest-hit area.
sentences.zh: 野火在美国西部正成为日益严重的威胁,其中南加州是受灾最严重的地区。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: There's a reason fire squads battling more frequent blazes in Southern California are having such difficulty containing the flames, despite better preparedness than ever and decades of experience fighting fires fanned by the 'Santa Ana Winds'.
sentences.zh: 尽管消防队比以往任何时候都做好了准备,并且拥有数十年扑灭“圣安娜风”引发的火灾的经验,但在南加州与更频繁的火灾作斗争的消防队却难以控制火势,这是有原因的。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.
sentences.zh: 专家表示,野火本身通常比过去更热、更快,而且蔓延更不稳定。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Megafires, also called 'siege fires', are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 500,000 acres or more - 10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 特大火灾,也称为“围城火灾”,是一种日益频繁的火灾,烧毁面积达 500,000 英亩或更多,是 20 年前平均森林火灾规模的 10 倍。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Some recent wildfires are among the biggest ever in California in terms of acreage burned, according to state figures and news reports.
sentences.zh: 根据州数据和新闻报道,就烧毁面积而言,最近发生的一些野火是加州有史以来最大的野火之一。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: One explanation for the trend to more superhot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years.
sentences.zh: 对超高温火灾趋势的一种解释是,该地区通常夏季干燥,但近年来降水量明显低于正常水平。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Another reason, experts say, is related to the century-long policy of the US Forest Service to stop wildfires as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 专家表示,另一个原因与美国林务局长达一个世纪的尽快阻止山火的政策有关。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of the underbrush, now the primary fuel for megafires.
sentences.zh: 无意中的后果是阻碍了灌木丛的自然消灭,而灌木丛现在是特大火灾的主要燃料。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Three other factors contribute to the trend, they add.
sentences.zh: 他们补充说,其他三个因素也促成了这一趋势。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: First is climate change, marked by a 1-degree Fahrenheit rise in average yearly temperature across the in western states.
sentences.zh: 首先是气候变化,其特点是西部各州年平均气温上升 1 华氏度。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 其次是火灾季节比 20 年前平均延长了 78 天。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.
sentences.zh: 第三是在林区增加房屋建设。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: 'We are increasingly building our homes in fire-prone ecosystems,' says Dominik Kulakowski, adjunct professor of biology at Clark University Graduate School of Geography in Worcester, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: “我们越来越多地在易发生火灾的生态系统中建造家园,”马萨诸塞州伍斯特市克拉克大学地理学研究生院生物学兼职教授多米尼克·库拉科斯基 (Dominik Ku​​lakowski) 说。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Doing that in many of the forests of the western US is like building homes on the side of an active volcano. '
sentences.zh: 在美国西部的许多森林中这样做就像在活火山边建造房屋一样。 '

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: In California, where population growth has averaged more than 600,000 a year for at least a decade, more residential housing is being built.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州,至少十年来人口平均每年增长超过 60 万,更多的住宅正在建设中。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: 'What once was open space is now residential homes providing fuel to make fires burn with greater intensity,' says Terry McHale of the California Department of Forestry firefighters' union.
sentences.zh: 加州林业部消防员工会的特里·麦克海尔 (Terry McHale) 表示,曾经的开放空间现在变成了住宅区,提供燃料,使火灾燃烧得更猛烈。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: 'With so much dryness, so many communities to catch fire, so many fronts to fight, it becomes an almost incredible job.'
sentences.zh: “由于如此干旱,如此多的社区着火,如此多的前线需要战斗,这几乎成为一项令人难以置信的工作。”

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: That said, many experts give California high marks for making progress on preparedness in recent years, after some of the largest fires in state history scorched thousands of acres, burned thousands of homes, and killed numerous people.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此,许多专家对加州近年来在备灾方面取得的进展给予高度评价,此前加州历史上一些最大的火灾烧毁了数千英亩土地,烧毁了数千所房屋,并造成无数人死亡。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Stung in the past by criticism of bungling that allowed fires to spread when they might have been contained, personnel are meeting the peculiar challenges of neighbourhood - and canyonhopping fires better than previously, observers
sentences.zh: 观察人士称,过去曾因对火势在本来可以得到控制的情况下仍蔓延开来的拙劣批评而感到刺痛,但工作人员正在应对邻里的特殊挑战,而且比以前更好地扑救火灾。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: State promises to provide more up-to-date engines, planes, and helicopters to fight fires have been fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 国家承诺提供更多最新的发动机、飞机和直升机来灭火,这一承诺已经兑现。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Firefighters' unions that in the past complained of dilapidated equipment, old fire engines, and insufficient blueprints for fire safety are now praising the state's commitment, noting that funding for firefighting has increased, despite huge cuts in many other programs.
sentences.zh: 过去抱怨设备破旧、消防车陈旧和消防安全蓝图不足的消防员工会现在赞扬国家的承诺,并指出尽管许多其他项目大幅削减,但用于消防的资金却有所增加。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: We are pleased that the current state administration has been very proactive in its support of us, and [has] come through with budgetary support of the infrastructure needs we have long sought,' says Mr. McHale of the firefighters' union.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴现任州政府非常积极地支持我们,并且[已经]为我们长期以来寻求的基础设施需求提供了预算支持,”消防员工会的麦克海尔先生说。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Besides providing money to upgrade the fire engines that must traverse the mammoth state and wind along serpentine canyon roads, the state has invested in better command-and-control facilities as well as in the strategies to run them.
sentences.zh: 除了提供资金升级必须穿越庞大的州并沿着蜿蜒的峡谷道路蜿蜒的消防车外,该州还投资了更好的指挥和控制设施以及运行它们的策略。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: 'In the fire sieges of earlier years, we found that other jurisdictions and states were willing to offer mutual-aid help, but we were not able to communicate adequately with them, says Kim Zagaris, chief of the state's Office of Emergency Services Fire and Rescue Branch. After a commission examined and revamped communications procedures, the state wide response 'has become far more professional and responsive,’ he says. There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past 'siege fire' situations.
sentences.zh: “在早年的火灾围困中,我们发现其他司法管辖区和州愿意提供互助帮助,但我们无法与他们充分沟通,”该州紧急服务办公室消防救援部门负责人金·扎加里斯(Kim Zagaris)说。他说,在委员会审查和修改了沟通程序后,全州范围内的反应“变得更加专业和反应迅速”。政府官员和居民都认为,来自多个州和司法管辖区的消防员的速度、奉献精神和协调使得效率比过去的“围攻火”情况更高。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: In recent years, the Southern California region has improved building codes, evacuation procedures, and procurement of new technology.
sentences.zh: 近年来,南加州地区改进了建筑规范、疏散程序和新技术的采购。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: 'I am extraordinarily impressed by the improvements we have witnessed,' says Randy Jacobs, a Southern Californiabased lawyer who has had to evacuate both his home and business to escape wildfires.
sentences.zh: 南加州律师兰迪·雅各布斯 (Randy Jacobs) 说,“我们所目睹的改善给我留下了极其深刻的印象”,他不得不撤离自己的家和公司以躲避野火。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: 'Notwithstanding all the damage that will continue to be caused by wildfires, we will no longer suffer the loss of life endured in the past because of the fire prevention and firefighting measures that have been put in place,' he says.
sentences.zh: “尽管野火将继续造成所有损失,但由于已经采取了防火和消防措施,我们将不再遭受过去遭受的生命损失,”他说。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

questions.title: Questions 1-13
instructions: Questions 7-13: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1 ?

items.prompt: At the end of paragraph 1, the writer indicates that “The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.”

At the beginning of paragraph 2, the writer says that “Megafires, also called “siege fires” are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 50,000 acres or more – 10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago.

In paragraph 3, the writer says that “One explanation for the trend to more super hot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years.”

In paragraph 3, “The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of underbrush, now the primary fuel for mega fires.” In the past, the US Forest Service had a policy of cutting this ‘brush’ – the plants that grow beneath the trees. However, the Service did not realize then that if this brush was eradicated naturally by fires, then this natural process would be more effective. Without realising this, as a result of their policy, the brush grew more quickly and strongly, providing more fuel to start fires.

In paragraph 4, the writer indicates that “Three other factors contribute to the trend, they add…Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago.” This means that fire seasons are extended.
At the end of paragraph 4, the writer says that “Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.”
The amount of open space in California has diminished over the last ten years.
Many experts believe California has made little progress in readying itself to fight fires.
Personnel in the past have been criticised for mishandling fire containment.
California has replaced a range of firefighting tools.
More firefighters have been hired to improve fire-fighting capacity.
Citizens and government groups disapprove of the efforts of different states and agencies working together.
Randy Jacobs believes that loss of life from fires will continue at the same levels, despite changes made.
